correctness.rationale: For fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), the maximal distance \(\pi\) occurs only for opposite poles. A uniform positive-quadrant bound on the local quadratic form gives \(O(\varepsilon)\) localization. Normalized area measures and both ordered pole configurations produce a factor 1/2. Polar substitution, tangent-variable integral J(c)=arccos(c)/sqrt(1-c^2), and a verified antiderivative give \(C(\alpha)\) exactly. Strict monotonicity follows by nested positive-quadrant ellipses; limits 1/48 and infinity establish invertibility. The round endpoint is computed separately. Exact arguments and deterministic quadrature agree; no inference from finite simulations is used as proof.

value.rationale: The sharp quartic diameter-tail constant is a geometrically natural observable on an entire continuous family of compact positively curved cone surfaces. It determines the total cone angle uniquely, has a distinct smooth-boundary exponent and an explicit discrete cyclic-quotient specialization. Determining one scalar coefficient solves a genuine inverse geometric-probability question rather than an arbitrary finite invariant.
